reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape; the rendered text is identical to the original paragraphs, so no invalid or directionally wrong edit was introduced.

The cited paragraphs support compliance: Section 11.2 allows termination for uncured material breach or insolvency with no minimum fee, acceleration or termination charge; the payment terms (p0166) show only actual maintenance and revenue-share fees with no penalty or stipulated sum payable by Corio (the licensee/customer).

The rationale correctly reasons that the Section 4.4 audit mechanic is a true-up of amounts actually owed plus reimbursement of reasonable examination costs, not a liquidated damages or penalty amount, so it does not trigger the rule (which applies only where Customer pays a stipulated sum).

Direction of the rule is respected: any response/resolution commitments run against Commerce One (Vendor), which the rule treats as compliant. No walk-away features (LDs exceeding remaining contract value or minor-breach triggers) are present, so retaining this as internal evidence rather than a negotiation issue is appropriate.
